headline: Highest risk is medium: shared filesystem and write access create prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict pathways; no direct evidence of stronger cross-agent coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read/write filesystem and its skills reference shared context; Agent B exposes a Superset API surface. A shared workspace or file handoff would let A’s content influence B, but no direct bridge is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are run against the same workspace or file tree
IF B ingests A-produced files or API payloads as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Require provenance tags on any A-produced file before B reads it
Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Review shared directories for prompt-like artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or policy filters at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches marketing content and product marketing context and can read/write files; B lists no data classes touched and no secrets. A shared workspace could leak A’s content into B, but the blast radius appears limited and B’s profile does not show default outbound file upload behavior.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or mounted workspace
IF B is configured to ingest local files into prompts or API calls
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Restrict B to read-only access where possible
Remove sensitive marketing drafts before cross-agent runs
Audit any file-to-prompt ingestion path
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries in the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has filesystem write and subprocess spawning; Agent B exposes a Superset API. Their mutable surfaces can overlap if they target the same workspace or API-backed state, creating race or overwrite risk. No locking is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared artifact store
IF B’s API actions mutate resources that A also edits locally
mitigations: Assign disjoint output paths
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Run one agent at a time for shared artifacts
Check for stale file timestamps before overwrite
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate marketing content and shared context; B can consume API-driven analytics workflows. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream decisions or published analytics. There is no documented verification step between them, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text, claims, or summaries as input
IF no human or automated verification occurs before B acts on A’s output
mitigations: Require a verification step before B consumes A output
Mark A output as draft-only
Compare A claims against source data before use
Limit B to read-only reporting until reviewed
requires-engineering: add validation rules for cross-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source marketing agent touching marketing context; B is Apache Superset with no declared sensitive data classes or residency constraints. No specific compliance mismatch is evidenced, but if A’s marketing files contain regulated personal data and B processes them, a policy gap could arise. The other agent is not cited because no residency or retention data is present.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into A’s marketing files
IF B stores or logs that data under a different retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of marketing artifacts
Review retention settings before shared use
Document data-class handling for both agents
Delete any accidental personal data from shared files
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across the pair
